questions.q: Why do consumers ignore most advertising today, according to the summary?
a: They have grown blind to ads and tune them out
Ads have become too expensive to produce
New laws limit what advertisers may claim
Most products sell out before ads appear
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the era after advertising, when people skip ads and trust word of mouth.

questions.q: What image does Godin use for a product that truly stands out?
a: A purple cow among ordinary cows
A loud billboard beside a busy road
A bargain bin in a discount store
A race car built purely for speed
questions.why: Lesson 2 says standing out in a noisy market is like being a purple cow in a herd of brown cows.

questions.q: Which company does the summary call steady but boring?
a: Ford, for barely changing over a decade
Porsche, for chasing risky new designs
Apple, for releasing a new phone each year
Nike, for spending heavily on athletes
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts Ford, which played it safe and saw its stock barely move, with Porsche.

questions.q: What risk did Porsche take with the 918 project?
a: It built a costly hybrid car and limited production to 918 units
It cut prices sharply to attract first-time buyers
It copied a rival's design to save development time
It delayed launch until the technology was proven
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes a hybrid supercar costing eight times normal models, capped at 918 cars.

questions.q: Who should a new product target first, according to the summary?
a: Innovators and early adopters
The cautious majority of buyers
Large retail chains and distributors
Government regulators and reviewers
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the majority wants a proven product, so early adopters must spread the word first.
